2. The case of the prosecution before the leaned trial Court was that deceased Mokbul had long-standing enmity with the appellants and their co-accused namely Azizul Huq alias Makhan, Abdul Jalil and Asgar Mistri ever various matters. On 22.5.87 PW 1 Khairul Islam was taking tea in a tea-stall at about 8-30 PM or 9-00 PM at Laldighi Bazar. His younger brother Firozuddin arrived there and took him out of the tea-stall and informed him that his father had been finished off. On receiving this information PW 1 Khairul Islam along with his younger brother Firozuddin advanced towards their house and when they were about 1/4 mile off from their house they found the dead body of their father Mokbul on an ail of a plot of land belonging to one Khoka Mia. They also found multiple injuries on the person of deceased Mokbul and it appeared to them that these injuries had been inflicted by some sharp weapons. A few days before 'the occurrence appellants Islam Mondal, Alam, Maznu, Samad, Shajahan, Abdur Rashid, Khawja, Ali, Dhonai, Sirajuddin, Moslemuddin and others had snatched away some money from the possession of deceased Mokbul Hossain and, as such, deceased Mokbul Hossain instituted a criminal case against them. The deceased, Mokbul, also filed an application under section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure against the appellant, All these cases were pending on the date of occurrence. The appellants and their co-accused were notorious miscreants and dacoits of the locality and were enraged on account of the cases instituted by deceased Mokbul and, as such, the appellants were supposed to have murdered deceased Mokbul on the date of occurrence. Many villagers also assembled at the place of occurrence and saw the dead body of deceased Mokbul. On the same day i.e. on 22.5.87 PW 1 Khairul Islam went to the Pirganj, PS at about 23.15 hours and lodged the first information report stating that he suspected the appellants and their co-accused to have committed the murder. PW 10 Motiar Rahman who was then Sub-Inspector of Police attached to Pirganj Police Station took up investigation of the case, visited the place of occurrence and held an inquest on the dead body of deceased Mokbul. He then forwarded the dead body to the morgue for post-mortem examination and PW 9 Dr. M. Bellah Azad held post mortem examination on the dead body of deceased Mokbul. PW 10 Motiar Rahman prepared sketch map of the place of occurrence along with an index, seized alamats, examined witnesses and after completing investigation submitted charge-sheet against the appellants and their co-accused. 

 9. There is no dispute in this case that on 22.5.87 Mokbul Hossain was murdered. In this connection, the evidence of PW 1. Khairul Islam, PW 9 Dr. M. Billah Azad and PW 10 Md. Motiar Rahman may be referred to. PW 1 Khairul Islam stated in his evidence that on receiving the information through his younger brother Firojuddin, he along with his younger brother proceeded towards his house from Laldighir Bazar tea stall and when they reached about mile off from their house they found their father lying dead with multiple injuries on his body in a piece of land belonging to one Khoka. The dead body was also seen by PW 2 Osman Ali, PW 3 Bablu, PW 4 Dablu and PW 7 Jamiruddin who corroborated PW 1 Khairul Islam about the discovery of the dead body of Mokbul Hossain at the place of occurrence. PW 10 Md. Motiar Rahman, the Investigating Officer, stated that he held inquest on the dead body of deceased Mokbul and forwarded the dead body to Rangpur morgue for post-mortem examination PW 9 Dr. M Billah Azad held post-mortem examination on the dead body of deceased Mokbul and his evidence shows that he found the following injuries on the person of deceased Mokbul : 

 12. In order to prove its case the prosecution produced 10 witnesses of whom 9 witnesses were examined and also cross-examined. 

 13. PW 1 Khairul Islam did not see the occurrence. He simply stated that on the date of occurrence on 22.5.87 at about 8-30 or 9-00 PM when he was sitting in a tea-stall at Laldighir Bazar his younger brother Firozuddin informed him that his father had been murdered and he proceeded along with his brother to their house and about 1/4 mile from the house he found the dead body of his father lying with multiple injuries on his person on the land of one Khoka. In his evidence, he did not state as to when, how or by whom the injuries had been inflicted on the body of deceased Mokbul causing his death. He also did not say that he saw any of the appellants and their co-accused to inflict the aforesaid injuries on the person of deceased Mokbul. There was enmity between his father, deceased Mokbul, and the appellants and their co-accused. Except the fact of enmity there is nothing in his evidence to show that the applicants and their co-accused assaulted the deceased and as a result of causing injuries by them he ultimately died. PW 2 Osman Ali stated in his evidence that on the date of occurrence at about 7-15 on 8-00 PM in the evening when he was sitting on the bank of the pond near Laldighi he saw appellants Islam, Ali, Dhonai, Samad, Siraj, Khawja, Maznu, Shahjahan, Alam, Rashid, Moslem and accused Makhan to drink wine sitting on the north bank of the pond. He also stated that at that time they were intoxicated and during their conversation he heard appellant Dhonai uttering that Mokbul ought to be murdered that day. He stated that after easing himself he went to Laldighir Bazar in search of Mokbul but could not find him out and then informed his son, PW 1 about it and asked him to be careful about his father. He also stated that after conversing with PW 1 he entered into the tea-stall and after he completed drinking of tea he heard an alarm to the east of the Bazar and went there and saw Mokbul lying dead in the land of one Khoka with multiple injuries on his person. He did not say whether he saw any of the appellant near the place of occurrence or as to whether any of the appellants had caused the injuries on the person of the deceased. Except the alleged utterance made by Dhonai to the effect that the chance to kill Mokbul must be availed there is nothing in his evidence to show that the appellants had .assaulted Mokbul thereby murdering him. PW 3 Bablu stated that on the date of occurrence at or about 8-00 or 8-30 PM he heard alarm while he was at his house. He also stated that he went out of the house and came to know that the father of PW 1 Khairul Islam had died. He also stated that he then went to the place of occurrence where the dead body was lying and saw the dead body of deceased Mokbul. There is, therefore, nothing in his evidence to show the involvement of the appellants in the murder of deceased Mokbul. In cross-examination he denied the suggestion made by the prosecution that he had seen the appellants to assault Mokbul and had recognized the appellants in the light of the hurricane which was carried by him. PW 4 Dablu stated in his examination-in-chief that he heard alarm in the evening of the date of occurrence at 7-30 or 8-00 PM and went out of the house and saw the dead body of Mokbul Hossain. He also did not implicate the appellants and their co-accused in the murder of deceased Mokbul. This witness was also declared hostile by the prosecution and was allowed to be cross-examined. In cross-examination he further denied the prosecution suggestion that he had seen Islam, Ali and Makhan to run away with stains of blood on their clothes. So there is nothing in his evidence to connect the appellants and their co-accused with the murder of deceased Mokbul Hossain. PW 5 Hafizur Rahman did not say anything as to the occurrence or the murder of Mokbul Hossain. He simply stated that he heard about the murder but did not go to see the dead body of Mokbul Hossain. He was declared hostile and was allowed to be cross examined. He denied the suggestion in cross examination that he has seen the appellants to run away from the place of occurrence. PW 6 Majed Ali was tendered by the prosecution. He was cross examined by the defence and in cross-examination he stated that the deceased, Mokbul, had enmity with various other people. PW 7 Jamiruddin stated that on the date of occurrence after the If tar time he was going to Laldighir Bazar with his son from his house and then he reached near the local primary school he found the appellants going towards Laldighir Bazar in rickshaw and bicycle and he also stated that he had heard appellant Islam Mondal to shout out that he along with his companions had gone to Salish at Union No.12. He also stated that he then went to Laldighir Bazar and after reaching Bazar he saw deceased Mokbul was standing in the tea-stall and he demanded some money which Mokbul owed to him. He also stated that after some time he came to know that Mokbul had been murdered. He did not state that he had seen the appellants whom he had met at Laldighir Bazar to assault and murder deceased Mokbul. His evidence also, therefore, does not prove the prosecution case regarding the involvement of the appellants and the accused in the murder of Mokbul. PW 8 Kazi Abdus . Sobhan happened to be a Magistrate. He appears to have been examined in order to prove certain statements recorded by him under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. From his evidence it appears that he recorded the statement of PW 2 Osman Ali, PW 3 Bablu, PW 4 Dablu and PW 5 Hafizur Rahman and it appears that the learned Additional Sessions Judge admitted these statements of the aforesaid persons recorded by PW 8 Kazi Abdus Sobhan into evidence. PW 9 Dr. M. Billah Azad was the Medical Officer who held autopsy on the dead body of Mokbul and PW 10 Md. Motian Rahman, as already stated, was the Investigation Officer. So from the above evidence it appears that there is virtually no evidence to connect the appellants with the occurrence alleged by the prosecution and with the commission of assault on the body of Mokbul on the dale of occurrence. 

 14. It further appears that despite any evidence adduced before the learned Additional Sessions Judge by the prosecution in support of its case that the appellants and their co-accused had assaulted deceased on 22.5.87 and ultimately cased his death, the learned Additional Sessions Judge convicted the appellants by depending on certain statements of PW 2 Osman Ali, PW 3 Bablu, PW 4 Dablu, PW 5 Hafizur Rahman and one Rashida Khatun who was not even examined at the trial Court. It appears that the learned Additional Sessions Judge, mainly relied on the statement of the said Rashida Khatun recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to the effect that she had seen the wife of one of the appellants, Islam Mondal, to wash blood stained clothes which appellant Islam Mondal had been wearing at the time of murder. He also appears to have relied on the statement of PW 3 Bablu and PW 4 Dablu recorded by PW 8 Kazi Abdus Sobhan under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and treating his statement as substantive evidence convicted the appellants by delivering the impugned judgment. It appears that the learned Additional Sessions Judge based his judgment on these statements recorded by PW 8 Kazi Abdus Sobhan under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. We regret to comment that the learned Additional Sessions Judge did not acquaint himself with the relevant provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Evidence Act before embarking upon the trial of a criminal case involving the highest penalty provided in the Penal Code A Judgment is the final decision based on proof of facts on consideration of the evidence adduced before the judge. As such, the judgment of a criminal court must be based on evidence and the evidence on which the judgment must be based is denied in section 3 of the Evidence Act which runs as follows: 

 The statements under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure recorded before an authority other than the learned Additional Sessions Judge who tried the instant case was not, therefore, the statement of the witnesses produced before him, and, as such, this could not be treated as oral evidence meant by sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Evidence Act. So, the statements treated by the learned additional Sessions Judge as evidence was not at all direct oral evidence adduced before him. These statements could not also he admitted into evidence under sub-section (2) of section 3 as substantive documentary evidence and these could only be used by the learned Additional Sessions Judge for such purpose as are mentioned in sections 145 and 157 of the Evidence Act, i.e. to contradict or corroborate a witness with reference to his previous statement. Such statements could not under any circumstances be used by the Court as substantive evidence for arriving at any finding as to the guilt or innocence of the accused. It is unfortunate that the learned Additional Sessions Judge also treated the statement of a person recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by a Magistrate as substantive evidence although the said person was not even examined before him. It, therefore, appears that by treating the statements of PW 2 Osman Ali, PW 3 Bablu, PW 4 Dablu and also one Rashida Khatun recorded by PW 8 Kazi Abdus Sobhan under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as substantive evidence and by basing his Judgment and order of conviction of the appellants on such statements the learned Additional Sessions Judge not only ignored the provisions of law but committed serious illegality. 

 18. The appellants are found not guilty of the charges under section 302 of the Penal Code read with section 34 of the Penal Code and they are, accordingly, acquitted thereof. All the appellants shall be set at liberty forthwith unless they are required in connection with any other case. 

 19. The connected Criminal Miscellaneous. Case No. 39 of 1990 regarding prayer for bail by the accused-appellants in Criminal Appeal No. 777 of 1991 is, accordingly, disposed of.
